summary: Iteration 4 — Google Auth session_token → session_id rename + new /auth deep-link route. Backend: 14/14 pytest PASS via public ingress. /api/auth/google-session with empty body → 422 detail='missing_session_id' (NEW). Same endpoint with bogus session_id → 401 detail='invalid_session_id' (RENAMED from invalid_session_token). Legacy alias session_token still accepted on the same endpoint and routes to the same Emergent verification, yielding the same 401 invalid_session_id. EMERGENT_AUTH_SESSION_URL env var is honored — set in /app/backend/.env (line 15) and confirmed via httpx call in backend logs (httpx GET → demobackend.emergentagent.com/auth/v1/env/oauth/session-data → 404 → mapped to 401). /api/auth/me, /api/auth/logout, /api/health, /api/parse-file, /api/subscription/{id}, /api/admin/login all regression-clean. Frontend: /auth route NO LONGER returns 'Page could not be found' (was the old bug). Visiting /auth without session_id quickly redirects to /login (Concluindo login... spinner displays briefly during the 500ms timeout, then router.replace('/') → ProtectedNav → /login since no auth). Visiting /auth?session_id=invalid_token_string_for_testing_123 triggers AuthProvider's web bootstrap → POST /api/auth/google-session {session_id: 'invalid...'} → 401 detail='invalid_session_id' captured in browser console as 'web session exchange failed Error: invalid_session_id' → URL session_id stripped via history.replaceState → ProtectedNav routes to /login showing 'Entrar com Google' button with testID=google-signin-button. The full new fault path is wired end-to-end exactly as described in the request. Real Google sign-in not attempted (requires real Google account interaction, per request).

rca_of_issue: Original user-reported defect ('Erro no login: invalid_session_token') was caused by the backend treating the Emergent-issued session_token (returned by client-side Emergent SDK) as if it were a session_id (X-Session-ID header expected by Emergent's session-data endpoint). The two-part fix is verified: (1) frontend now posts the raw session_id received from the OAuth redirect URL to /api/auth/google-session, (2) backend GET to EMERGENT_AUTH_SESSION_URL with X-Session-ID: <session_id> exchanges for the user profile, mapping non-200 responses to 401 detail='invalid_session_id'. The new /auth Expo route is now public (added to publicScreens) so deep-link callbacks no longer 404. All behavior verified by 14 backend pytest cases and live Playwright end-to-end exchange.
